title: Pulling back a Yoneda prefix and replacing its short exact tail
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. A degree-$r$ Yoneda extension of $U$ by $V$, for $r\geq1$, means an exact sequence $0\to V\to X_{r-1}\to\cdots\to X_0\to U\to0$. Equivalence means the relation generated by morphisms of these sequences fixing both endpoints. Let $n\geq2$ and let $\xi$ be an $n$-extension $0\to T\to E_{n-1}\to\cdots\to E_1\to E_0\xrightarrow{e}F\to0$. Put $L=\ker(e)$, and let $p:P\to E_0$ be a morphism for which $ep:P\to F$ is epic. Set $K=\ker(ep)$; the induced map $a:K\to L$ is determined by the kernel inclusions and $p$. The prefix ending in $L$ is an $(n-1)$-extension. Its pullback along $a$, obtained by replacing $E_1$ by $E_1\times_L K$ and using the zero $K$-component on the incoming map, is an exact $(n-1)$-extension $\eta$ of $K$ by $T$. Splice $\eta$ with the short exact sequence $0\to K\to P\xrightarrow{ep}F\to0$, using $E_1\times_L K\to K\to P$ for the joining arrow. The splice is an exact $n$-extension of $F$ by $T$. Projection $E_1\times_L K\to E_1$, the map $p:P\to E_0$, and identities on every other term define a morphism from this splice to $\xi$, fixing $T$ and $F$. In particular the splice and $\xi$ are Yoneda equivalent. No projective or injective objects are assumed.

source.place: Tag 06XT (definition-yoneda-extension); prefix pullback and endpoint-fixing comparison in Section 06XP; the pullback construction is Homology section-extensions. Agent-formulated exact-sequence comparison for the inherited step 8.

proof.text: Write $\ell:L\to E_0$ and $i:K\to P$ for the kernel inclusions. The arrow $E_1\to E_0$ factors uniquely as $\ell d$ for $d:E_1\to L$. Exactness at $E_0$ makes $d$ epic by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-iff-epi-kernel-lift]. Since $\ell$ is monic, a morphism into $E_1$ is killed by $d$ if and only if it is killed by $\ell d$. Thus replacing the final arrow of the prefix by $d$ preserves its preceding kernel and all earlier exactness. Together with $d$ epic, this proves that the prefix ending in $L$ is an $(n-1)$-extension. The same criterion applied to $K\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{ep}F$ gives exactness at $P$, since the induced arrow to $\ker(ep)=K$ is $1_K$; $i$ is monic and $ep$ is epic by hypothesis, so its zero-augmented sequence is short exact. Finally $epi=0$ gives a unique $a:K\to L$ with $\ell a=pi$.

source.place: Tag 010E (definition-exact); kernel universal property; the exactness-to-kernel criterion used in the construction of extensions, Tag 010I (section-extensions).

proof.text: Form $Q=E_1\times_L K$ with projections $r:Q\to E_1$, $s:Q\to K$, so $dr=as$. Explicitly take $Q=\ker((d,-a):E_1\oplus K\to L)$: maps $W\to Q$ correspond uniquely to pairs $(x:W\to E_1,y:W\to K)$ with $dx=ay$. This proves existence and the pullback universal property from the biproduct and kernel in [def-sp-abelian]. Let $D=T$ and $b:T\to E_1$ be the original first arrow if $n=2$; if $n>2$, let $D=E_2$ and $b:E_2\to E_1$ be the original differential. In either case $db=0$, hence there is a unique $j:D\to Q$ with $rj=b$ and $sj=0$. Use $j$ as the new incoming arrow. For $n>2$ its composite with the preceding differential vanishes, since both projections of that composite vanish.

source.place: Tag 05PJ (example-fibre-product-pushouts), part (1): fibre product as kernel of the difference map; Tag 010I (section-extensions), pullback construction.

proof.text: The projection $s$ is epic. Indeed, for any $y:W\to K$, the epimorphism $d$ and [lem-sp-abelian-refinements](a) give an epimorphism $\rho:W\prime\to W$ and $x:W\prime\to E_1$ with $dx=ay\rho$. The pair $(x,y\rho)$ gives $z:W\prime\to Q$ with $sz=y\rho$. Applying (a) once more, now to $s$, proves the claim. This is the three-line refinement proof of stability under pullback (Tag 05PK), so no additional pullback lemma is needed.

source.place: Tag 05PK (lemma-epimorphism-universal-abelian-category), part (1); formulation by refinements as in Tag 08N5 (lemma-check-exactness-fibre-product).

proof.text: Exactness at $Q$ follows from [lem-sp-abelian-refinements](b), rather than from element chasing in a concrete category. For $z:W\to Q$ with $sz=0$, one has $drz=asz=0$. The original exactness at $E_1$, with incoming arrow $b:D\to E_1$, gives an epimorphism $\rho:W\prime\to W$ and $t:W\prime\to D$ such that $bt=rz\rho$. Both projections of $jt$ and $z\rho$ agree: their $r$-projections are $bt=rz\rho$, and their $s$-projections are zero. Therefore $jt=z\rho$, proving exactness of $D\xrightarrow{j}Q\xrightarrow{s}K$ by (b).

source.place: Tag 08N5 (lemma-check-exactness-fibre-product): exactness tested by lifts after epimorphic refinement; applied to the pullback of Tag 010I (section-extensions).

proof.text: Check the remaining terms of $\eta$. If $n=2$, $j:T\to Q$ is monic because $rj=b$ is the monomorphism $T\to E_1$: $ju=jv$ implies $bu=bv$, hence $u=v$. Thus the sequence $0\to T\xrightarrow{j}Q\xrightarrow{s}K\to0$ is exact. If $n>2$, $jt=0$ is equivalent to $bt=0$ for every morphism $t$ into $E_2$: one implication follows by applying $r$, and the other from the two projections $rjt=bt=0$, $sjt=0$. Hence $\ker j=\ker b$ as subobjects of $E_2$, so original exactness at $E_2$ gives new exactness there. All terms further left, including the monic left endpoint, are unchanged. With Steps 3 and 4 this proves every exactness assertion for $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 010E (definition-exact); Tag 010I (section-extensions), explicit kernel check for the pullback.

proof.text: Splice by taking the joining arrow $is:Q\to P$. Because $i$ is monic, $ist=0$ if and only if $st=0$ for every morphism $t$ into $Q$. Its kernel is therefore $\ker s$, so exactness at $Q$ is Step 4. At $P$, the incoming map to $\ker(ep)=K$ is $s$, which is epic by Step 3; [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-iff-epi-kernel-lift] gives exactness there. All terms left of $Q$ have already been checked, and $ep$ is epic. Consequently this is an exact $n$-extension of $F$ by $T$.

source.place: Tag 06XT (definition-yoneda-extension); Tag 06XP (section-ext), concatenation of Yoneda extensions; explicit exactness at the join.

proof.text: Take the comparison to $\xi$ to be $r$ at $Q$, $p$ at $P$, and identities elsewhere. The incoming square at $Q$ is $rj=b$ by construction; this also checks the $T$-endpoint square when $n=2$. The joining square commutes because $p(is)=(pi)s=(\ell a)s=\ell(dr)=(\ell d)r$. The right endpoint square is $ep=ep$, with identity on $F$. When $n>2$ the $T$-endpoint and all other squares are identities on unchanged arrows. Thus this is a morphism of exact extensions fixing both endpoints. By the stated definition of Yoneda equivalence, this single morphism proves the splice equivalent to $\xi$; no Ext comparison, resolutions, or projective or injective objects are used.

lean.statement: theorem pullback_splice_equivalent {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] {T F : A} (n : ℕ) (E : YonedaExtension A T F (n + 2)) (e : E.sequence.obj' (n + 2) ⟶ F) (he : E.sequence.map' (n + 2) (n + 3) ≫ E.rightIso.hom = e) (P : A) (p : P ⟶ E.sequence.obj' (n + 2)) [Epi (p ≫ e)] : ∃ (d : E.sequence.obj' (n + 1) ⟶ kernel e) (a : kernel (p ≫ e) ⟶ kernel e) (B : YonedaExtension A T (kernel e) (n + 1)) (t : B.sequence.δlast ≅ E.sequence.δlast.δlast) (H : YonedaExtension A T (kernel (p ≫ e)) (n + 1)) (b : H.sequence ⟶ B.sequence) (G : YonedaExtension A T F (n + 2)) (s : RightSplice (ShortComplex.mk (kernel.ι (p ≫ e)) (p ≫ e) (kernel.condition (p ≫ e))) H G) (φ : G.sequence ⟶ E.sequence), d ≫ kernel.ι e = E.sequence.map' (n + 1) (n + 2) ∧ a ≫ kernel.ι e = kernel.ι (p ≫ e) ≫ p ∧ t.hom.app 0 ≫ E.leftIso.hom = B.leftIso.hom ∧ B.sequence.map' (n + 1) (n + 2) ≫ B.rightIso.hom = t.hom.app (Fin.last (n + 1)) ≫ d ∧ (ShortComplex.mk (kernel.ι (p ≫ e)) (p ≫ e) (kernel.condition (p ≫ e))).ShortExact ∧ H.leftMap B b = 𝟙 T ∧ H.rightMap B b = a ∧ (∀ k : Fin (n + 3), k.val < n + 1 → IsIso (b.app k)) ∧ IsPullback (b.app ⟨n + 1, by omega⟩) (H.sequence.map' (n + 1) (n + 2) ≫ H.rightIso.hom) (B.sequence.map' (n + 1) (n + 2) ≫ B.rightIso.hom) a ∧ (∀ k : Fin (n + 2), s.prefixIso.hom.app k ≫ φ.app k.castSucc.castSucc = b.app k.castSucc ≫ t.hom.app k) ∧ s.lastIso.hom ≫ ComposableArrows.app' φ (n + 2) = p ∧ G.leftMap E φ = 𝟙 T ∧ G.rightMap E φ = 𝟙 F ∧ G.Equivalent E
